questions.stem: What happens when blood glucose levels fall below normal?

options.text: The pancreas releases insulin to lower glucose further
The kidneys remove excess glucose in urine
The pancreas releases glucagon, which causes the liver to convert glycogen back into glucose
The liver converts glucose into glycogen

questions.explanation: When blood glucose is too low, the pancreas releases glucagon. Glucagon causes the liver to break down its glycogen stores into glucose, which is released into the blood to raise glucose levels.
